gaps.sentence: This new timetable will mean ___ earlier trains.
It was kind of them ___ us a lift to the station.
gaps.explanation: 'It was kind of them to give …' — to-infinitive after the adjective.

gaps.sentence: It's not worth ___ about the delay — nothing will change.
I tried ___ the shelf up, but it was too heavy.
gaps.explanation: try + to-infinitive = attempt, make an effort.

gaps.sentence: The rules don't ___ visitors to touch the paintings.
gaps.explanation: allow + object + to-infinitive: allow visitors to touch. (let + bare: let visitors touch.)

gaps.sentence: I saw him ___ the wall and disappear into the garden.
gaps.explanation: see/hear + object + bare infinitive = the complete action; -ing = the action in progress. Both readings possible here; the bare infinitive is expected.

gaps.sentence: We spent the whole morning ___ for tickets.
gaps.explanation: spend time + -ing: spent the morning queueing.

gaps.sentence: Remember ___ your passport to the airport.
gaps.explanation: remember + to-infinitive = not forget to do something.
